name: js_array_buffer_layout
prototype: JSValue obj; void *abuf = *(void **)(obj + 32); data = *(void **)abuf; detached = *(u8 *)(abuf + 4); byte_length = *(u32 *)(abuf + 8);

ownership.argument: Array buffer field layout as the engine itself reads it, from JS_GetArrayBuffer 0xC2D362C: it accepts tag -1 with class 19 or 20 (ArrayBuffer / SharedArrayBuffer), takes the buffer pointer from object+32, rejects it when the byte at abuf+4 is non-zero ("ArrayBuffer is detached"), and returns data = *(u32*)abuf and byte_length = *(u32*)(abuf+8). The typed-array path 0xC2D368C reaches the same struct through its own indirection and reports the same "ArrayBuffer is detached" error.

provenance.source: Producer/consumer pair: JS_GetArrayBuffer 0xC2D362C reads the fields, and JS_NewArrayBuffer 0xC2D34C8 writes them (byte length at abuf+0 in the constructor is the allocation size word, detached flag cleared with *((_WORD *)v14 + 2) = 0 at abuf+4). The earlier device measurement that put the payload at object+0x54 was reading the wrong object; the engine-visible layout is the one above.

notes: ARRAY_BUFFER_DETACHED is therefore the byte at abuf+4 (non-zero = detached), not a bit in a flags word; the constructor clears it with a 16-bit store, which covers both it and the shared flag byte in one go. Typed arrays reach the same buffer through their own indirection, which is not yet measured.
